items.title: Allan Jaffe Interview, 1969-04-16
items.q: Tom Decker, his human and Russell, came over for the first time.

ctx.x: Well, can we touch the subject side to the actual musical aspects of the hall and the people that you were, how you decided to go about choosing a particular band and particularly is to be used in a book about George Lewis. What sort of role do you feel that George played in the development of the hall and it's, you know, kind of working out? He was one of the, you know, few musicians whose name I knew before I came here. You know, the people, you know, involved with the punk band, you know, records I heard, of…
Tom Decker, his human and Russell, came over for the first time.

And, right when the hall started, George left town. And he never played at the hall, you know, when it was actually a hall. And he was, the first time he really started playing, he came back from a trip. Where'd he go in, 61? I think he went. To Europe? To the Dardy Tate. Yeah. Yeah. He came back. He came over, came over here, went back, and I asked him if he would like to bring in a band. And he said, no, he would rather, you know, be a sideman. So he started playing with Thomas' band. And, oh, he played with…
